slices.label: Uncontrolled commands
slices.question: Why could one command reach every case, unchecked?

slices.label: Who did it
slices.question: Why can't we name who sent it?

slices.label: AI that can be steered
slices.question: Why did the assistant say warm stock was fine?

slices.label: Nobody owns it
slices.question: Why did every control assume another control?

fixes.title: Alarm on temperature and time, in any mode
fixes.what: A case above its limit for too long raises an alarm, even during defrost.
fixes.risk: Pages planned defrosts if it ignores the defrost schedule, and false pages cost money and trust.

fixes.title: Defrost guardrail
fixes.what: A defrost with no end time, or longer than allowed, is refused or ends on its own.
fixes.risk: Refusing a long but planned vendor defrost blocks maintenance and brings the vendor back.

fixes.title: Command limits on setpoints
fixes.what: Setpoints outside a safe range for the case type are refused.
fixes.risk: Ranges set too tight block legitimate seasonal changes.

fixes.title: Fleet-command hold with human approval
fixes.what: A command to many cases at once waits until a named person approves it.
fixes.risk: Every held planned command costs a vendor revisit, and someone has to be on call at night to approve.

fixes.title: Audit trail: who sent every command
fixes.what: Every command records who sent it, when and to which cases.
fixes.risk: Names a shared account, not a person, until vendor accounts are separated.

fixes.title: Safe-answer rule for the store assistant
fixes.what: The assistant answers from the temperature history, says unknown when unsure, and ignores instructions in notes.
fixes.risk: Too cautious and staff stop asking; too trusting and it calls warm stock fine.

fixes.title: Named vendor accounts and approved windows
fixes.what: Each vendor engineer signs in as themselves, only inside an approved change window.
fixes.risk: Needs the vendor contract reopened (ZFW-203). Policy and contract work, so the Gauntlet can't measure it.

fixes.title: Owners and a current pager list
fixes.what: Every system area has a named owner, and the pager list is checked monthly.
fixes.risk: A process change, not code: it decays unless someone owns it. The Gauntlet can't measure it.
